ListItems.Title: Crocodile Museum
ListItems.Description:
The Crocodile Museum is located next to the Kom Ombo temple, north of Aswan. This museum has highlighted the crocodile-headed god Sobek since it was opened in 2012. Its main exhibition hall displays the mummified mummies of Nile crocodiles. The longest crocodile was 4.30 m, while the smallest was 2 m.

ListItems.Title: The Crocodile Museum anniversary
ListItems.Description:
The Crocodile Museum celebrated its 12th anniversary since opening, which falls on January 31st of each year.
During the celebration, a scientific symposium was organised to introduce the museum and its collection.
The museum also organised a drawing workshop for children, introductory guided tours for visitors, and honoured the distinguished employees of the museum.

ListItems.Title: Mummification Museum
ListItems.Description:
Mummification museum in Luxor (ancient Thebes), intended to provide an understanding of the process to preserve the body. The ancient Egyptians not only applied embalming to dead humans but also to many animals (Cats, dogs, crocodiles…. etc.). God Anubis(the Jackal) was the god of embalming and mummification.

ListItems.Description:
Today we take you on a virtual tour in one of the oldest museums in the Middle East, the Zoological Museum, at the Giza Zoo.Where you can see rare skeletons and mummified models of various animals, birds and wild reptiles. ListItems.Title: Canopic Jars of Isetemkheb
ListItems.Description:
During the mummification process, certain organs of the deceased, namely the liver, lungs, intestines and stomach, would be mummified, wrapped separately and then placed in four “canopic” jars.

ListItems.Title: The Netherworld
ListItems.Description:
THE NETHERWORLD 
Afterlife played an important role in the ancient Egyptian beliefs. The River Nile as well as the agricultural cycle had contributed to their beliefs about rebirth and resurrection. When the deceased cross over to the netherworld known as “Duat” in the ancient Egyptian language, they were reborn again and placed on Ra’s solar boat in order to emerge with him in the day. ListItems.Title: Gebel al-Silsila
ListItems.Description: Gebel al-Silsila is a mountainous region with sandstone quarries on both sides of the Nile. The sandstone quarries of Gebel al-Silsila have been used from the Middle Kingdom (c. 2034–1650 BC) until the 20th century. ListItems.Title: The work of the Egyptian archaeological mission in Wadi Abu Saubeira
ListItems.Description: The work of the Egyptian archaeological mission in Wadi Abu Subeira in the Eastern desert northeast of Aswan, uncovered a series of royal rock inscriptions.
